full_judgment:
2. The short facts leading to the issuance of this Rule are that the landed property of House No. CWN(B)-30, (Holding No. 117, Gulshan Model Town) was a DIT (Dhaka Improvement Trust) plot and the same was allotted in favour of one Ali Mohammad Abbas on the basis of a lease deed 28-9-1961 (Annexure-A). The said allottee constructed a two-storied building thereon. The said owner, Ali Mohammad Abbas, entered into a contract with the petitioner and executed a bainapatra on 28-2-1971 at a consideration of Taka 80,000.00 to sell the disputed property of the said consideration money Taka 40,000.00 was paid on the same date and the petitioner was given delivery of possession of the property. The said property was enlisted as abandoned property by the government in list 'Ka' and the same was notified in the Bangladesh Gazette on 23-9-1986 vide serial No. 9762 (Annexure-B). Ali Mohammad Abbas was a practicing Barrister-at-Law and used to live in Great Britain (UK). As he was not executing and registering the sale deed in respect of the property in question in favour of the petitioner, the petitioner as plaintiff filed Title Suit No. 54 of 1986 on 17-2-1986 in the First Court of Subordinate Judge, Dhaka against Ali Mohammad Abbas, the Chairman of the DIT and the Government of Bangladesh represented by the Secretary, Ministry of Public Works for specific performance of contract and also for a decree for declaring that the enlistment of the case property as abandoned property was void and illegal. Summons was issued upon Ali Mohammad Abbas but it was returned unserved and the petitioner came to learn that he died in London on 16-6-1979. The petitioner thereafter substituted the heirs of Ali Mohammad Abbas in the said suit vide order dated 21-6-1989. The substituted heirs of Ali Mohammad Abbas, DIT and the Government having entered appearance contested the suit by filing separate written statements. During pendency of the suit the petitioner filed a case, being No. 176 of 1987 (Ka-21-Gulshan Area, Dhaka) in the First Court of Settlement, Bangladesh Abandoned Buildings, Dhaka praying for exclusion of the property .in question from 'Ka' 'list of the abandoned buildings. During the pendency of the case in the Court of Settlement, Title Suit No. 54 of 1986 was transferred to the Commercial Court, Dhaka wherein the same was renumbered as Title Suit No. 35 of 1992. The suit was dismissed on contest by the judgment and decree dated 20-10-1994. Against the said judgment and decree, the petitioner filed Title Appeal No. 378 of 1994 in the Court of District judge, Dhaka. The heirs of Late Ali Mohammad Abbas filed an appeal, being Title Appeal No. 399 of 1994. During pendency of the aforesaid two appeals, the Court of Settlement by the judgment and order dated 7-8-1995 dismissed the case, holding that the property had rightly been enlisted as abandoned property. 

 5. Mr SS Halder, learned Advocate for the petitioner, submits that the case property cannot be enlisted as abandoned unless it is proved that the citizenship of the original owner was cancelled or that his activities were prejudicial to the interest of Bangladesh. He submits that from Annexures-E and F it appears that the citizenship of the original owner was never cancelled. He next submits that before enlisting the case property as abandoned the writ petitioner filed a suit for specific performance of contract and succeeded in obtaining a decree for specific performance of contract from the appellate Court and as such enlisting of the case property as abandoned property was illegal and without jurisdiction. 

 9. The next contention of the learned Advocate for the petitioner as to obtaining a decree for specific performance of contract from the appellate Court is of no avail as the Government is not bound by a decree passed in a suit for specific performance of contract. In this connection reliance may be made in the case of CQM Md Ayub Ali vs Bangladesh 47 DLR (AD) 71. The relevant portion of the judgment of the said case is as follows: 

 "The decree in a suit for specific performance of contract will show that it has only decided the controversy between the vendor and the vendee and directed the vendor to execute the necessary document in favour of the vendee. I have, therefore, no hesitation to hold that such a decree is not the one which is mentioned in proviso (a) and, as such, the existence of such a decree cannot be pleaded as a bar for inclusion of the building in the list." 

 11. As to the date of filing of Title Suit for specific performance of contract there is also anomaly. The appellate Court in its judgment (page-22 of the judgment annexed with the application for injunction filed by the Writ Petitioner) observed, that the suit was filed on 12-9-1986 i.e. after publication of the Gazette Notification and listing of the property as abandoned. But from the certified copy of the decree of Title Suit No. 135 of 1992 it appears that the suit was filed on 17-2-86 i.e. before publication of the Gazette Notification. Having considered this aspect, the Court of Settlement came to the finding that unless the entire order sheet was filed the actual date of filing of the suit could not be ascertained.
